targetWords.definition: To cater to someone means to provide them with all the things needed or wanted.
targetWords.example: Bill was too sick to get out of bed, so his nurse catered to his needs.

targetWords.definition: When someone is considerate, they pay attention to the needs of others.
targetWords.example: The considerate boy gave a present to his girlfriend on Valentine's Day.

targetWords.definition: The consumption of food or drink is the act of eating or drinking it.
targetWords.example: These apples are too rotten for consumption.

targetWords.definition: Criteria are factors on which a person judges or decides something.
targetWords.example: Before she got the job, she had to meet all the necessary criteria.

targetWords.definition: Crust is the tough outer part of a loaf of bread.
targetWords.example: The little boy never ate the crust of his pizza.

targetWords.definition: To degrade someone means to cause people to have shame.
targetWords.example: The teacher degraded Bob when she announced his poor performance to the class

targetWords.definition: To entitle someone means to give them the rights to have or do something.
targetWords.example: His golden ticket entitled him to sit in the front row at the concert.

targetWords.definition: To escort people means to safely accompany them to a place.
targetWords.example: Her bodyguards escorted her to the movie theater.

story.title: The Old Hound
story.passage:
Elvis was a dog that loved to run. He possessed all the criteria to be a great racing dog.

He had long legs, lean muscles, and a strong heart. He was so good that he never lost a

race in the northern hemisphere. Spectators who bet on dog races always picked Elvis to

win.

After ten years of racing, however, Elvis was getting old. His faculties were not as strong

as they used to be. His owner got upset when Elvis started losing. Elvis's owner wasn't a

considerate person. He degraded the dog all the time. Finally, his owner decided to get rid

of him. He threw Elvis in his car and took him to the middle of the forest. He tossed him out

and drove away. Elvis was cold and scared. He decided to follow a brook into the city.

Elvis soon found out that the city was a big and impersonal place. Everywhere he went,

he saw signs that said, "No Dogs Allowed." Pedestrians yelled at him. He was sad, hungry,
